Recent environmental change shapes biotic homogenisation of Orthoptera and Mantodea communities in semi-dry grasslands
items.samenvatting_bron: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment of traditional management. While declines of specialised insects have repeatedly been reported, the extent to which these drivers promote long-term community reorganisation and biotic homogenisation remains poorly understood. Using a nationwide resurvey of 221 semi-dry grassland patches across Germany, spanning two to three decades, we investigated long-term changes in Orthoptera and Mantodea communities. We quantified changes in species richness, community composition, and beta diversity, and related these patterns to major global change drivers. Despite an increase in total species richness, these communities became increasingly homogenised, as indicated by declining beta diversity. Community reorganisation was characterised by pronounced winner-loser dynamics, with highly mobile generalists and thermophilous species expanding, whereas threatened species, low-mobility habitat specialists, and species associated with High Nature Value farmland declined. Winner species richness increased particularly in warm and dry regions, under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and outside protected areas. items.titel: LACK OF GREEN AREAS AND CHILDREN'S SCREEN TIME IN URBAN PERIPHERIES: SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES IN LIGHT OF THE SDG
items.samenvatting_bron: The advance of urbanization in recent decades has brought profound transformations to the social and environmental dynamics of Brazilian cities. Among its most noticeable effects is growing socio-spatial inequality, expressed in the concentration of infrastructure and services in central areas, while the outskirts remain lacking in public facilities and green spaces. This lack directly impacts opportunities for leisure, socialization, and contact with nature, particularly impacting urban children. At the same time, the intensive use of digital technologies has transformed the ways we play, learn, and interact. Children from different social backgrounds spend increasingly more time in front of screens, a phenomenon that, although it has educational and cultural dimensions, takes on the contours of a public health problem when it replaces physical activities, outdoor play, and social interactions. The COVID-19 pandemic has intensified this trend, increasing the time spent on electronic devices and further reducing access to public spaces. The combination of a lack of green infrastructure and increased screen time reflects not only behavioral changes but also structural inequalities that limit children's right to the city and nature. items.titel: Urbanization, Habitat Fragmentation, and Vector-Borne Disease Emergence
items.samenvatting_bron: Rapid urbanization and habitat fragmentation increasingly contribute to the growing burden of vector-borne diseases, particularly in expanding urban settings. This chapter examines how urban ecological change, environmental determinants, and socioeconomic conditions interact to shape disease emergence and transmission, with implications for public health and sustainable urban planning. Altered breeding habitats, urban microclimates, and biodiversity loss enhance the proliferation of vectors such as mosquitoes and ticks, while factors including population density, housing quality, sanitation, and healthcare access influence exposure and vulnerability. The chapter emphasizes integrated vector ecology and health risk assessment, highlighting the use of digital tools, geographic information systems, and remote sensing for environmental monitoring and disease surveillance. Policy-oriented strategies, green infrastructure, and community-based preventive approaches are discussed alongside key challenges.

items.titel: Two Decades of Landscape Connectivity Science: a Bibliometric Analysis of Thematic Structure, Temporal Trajectories, and the Ecological Security Divide
items.samenvatting_bron: Landscape connectivity is a central organizing concept of spatial ecology and conservation, but the breadth of systems, methods, and disciplines invoking the term obscures its intellectual structure. This study maps that structure empirically to reveal the field’s principal divisions and their trajectories. I applied bag-of-words multivariate clustering, redundancy analysis (RDA), random forest machine learning, and multivariate trajectory analysis to 6,280 landscape-connectivity papers from the Web of Science Core Collection, examining hierarchical clusters at five levels (2, 3, 6, 12, and 18 clusters). The deepest division in the field is not methodological but framework-based: a compact, rapidly growing cluster of “ecological security pattern” planning papers—concentrated in China and built on a state-led, source–corridor–node, composite-index idiom—separates from the rest of connectivity science, distinguished by a random forest with 97.7% accuracy on words including ECOLOGICAL, SECURITY, SOURCES, CORRIDORS, PATTERN, and CHINA. items.titel: Spatial patterns of reptile road mortality in a coastal landscape of the Río de la Plata, Argentina
items.samenvatting_bron: Road mortality is a major threat to vertebrate populations worldwide, yet its spatial patterns remain poorly documented for many taxonomic groups and regions. In particular, information on the spatial distribution of reptile road mortality is scarce in temperate coastal landscapes of southern South America. We analyzed reptile road mortality records obtained through systematic surveys conducted between 2019 and 2025, complemented by museum specimens (2000–2022) and citizen science records (2013–2025), along a 249-km coastal corridor of the Río de la Plata, Argentina. Using kernel density estimation, we evaluated the spatial patterns of road mortality and identified areas with high concentrations of roadkill events. A total of 191 road-killed reptiles belonging to 17 species were recorded, with snakes accounting for the majority of individuals. Road mortality was spatially concentrated in four well-defined hotspots, which differed in species richness and diversity. These results provide a baseline assessment of reptile road mortality in a coastal landscape and highlight priority areas for monitoring and management along the studied road corridor.

items.titel: Baseline chemical properties and biodiversity monitoring using environmental DNA in the Eastern Shore Islands Area of Interest
items.samenvatting_bron: The Eastern Shore Islands (ESI) form a uniquely dense archipelago of islands, coastal features, and diverse subtidal habitats on the Eastern Shore of Nova Scotia (NS). This physical and ecological diversity led to the identification of the area as an Area of Interest (AOI) for potential designation as a Marine Protected Area under Canada’s Oceans Act. To support a holistic understanding of the AOI and to inform future management, we collected baseline physical and chemical oceanographic data and environmental DNA (eDNA) samples along four transects extending from nearshore environments to the outer bounds of the AOI, characterizing habitat conditions and the biodiversity they support. Follow-up eDNA sampling in 2022 and 2023 established a time series to track changes in fish, invertebrate, and algal communities. items.titel: Wildlife Under Pressure
items.samenvatting_bron: Wildlife is facing unprecedented threats from human activities, including habitat destruction, climate change, pollution, illegal wildlife trade, overexploitation, and human–wildlife conflict. These pressures are accelerating biodiversity loss, disrupting ecosystem functions, and reducing the resilience of natural environments. This chapter examines the major anthropogenic drivers of wildlife decline and evaluates contemporary conservation strategies for safeguarding biodiversity. It highlights the role of protected areas, habitat restoration, community-based conservation, ecological corridors, and stronger policy frameworks in promoting sustainable wildlife management. The chapter also explores the application of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, drones, camera traps, and environmental DNA (eDNA) for wildlife monitoring, anti-poaching initiatives, and evidence-based conservation planning.

items.titel: Otters appear to have declined throughout Ireland amid increased pressures on water quality, but remain ubiquitous
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Governments must report on the conservation status of species designated as protected. We assessed changes in the Near Threatened Eurasian otter Lutra lutra population throughout Ireland (the whole island) from the 1980s to the 2020s using four National Otter Surveys (6,060 sites surveyed) and citizen science data (10,980 records). In 2023–2024, otters were recorded at 65% (95% CI 62–68%) of sites in the Republic of Ireland and 66% (95% CI 58–74%) of sites in Northern Ireland. Rivers, lakes and coasts were included in the surveys. Long-term trends in the population estimate indicate a decline of 24−27% (or 3−18% after correction for negative methodological biases). Short-term trends indicated changes of −7% to +2% in the Republic of Ireland and −26% to −27% in Northern Ireland. Otters remain widespread, having been recorded in 95% of hectads (10 × 10 km squares), with no range reduction. They prefer wide, fast-flowing rivers with rocky substrates, unmaintained banks, and riparian woodlands (trees and shrubs), and are positively associated with angling (probably because of salmonid prey) but negatively with peatlands. Eleven pressures were identified, notably site disturbance, including agricultural pollution, siltation and water abstraction, which increased over time. No single pressure threatens otters nationally, but cumulative effects on water quality and ecosystems likely contributed to the decline. items.titel: Aboveground biomass, carbon stock, and economic valuation of a tiny forest in a small Brazilian City
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Urban forests have gained increasing attention as nature-based solutions, yet quantitative information on aboveground biomass and carbon storage in small urban forest remnants remains limited, particularly in small municipalities. This study aimed to quantify aboveground biomass, carbon stocks, and their illustrative economic valuation in an urban Tiny Forest located in southeastern Brazil. A complete tree inventory was conducted across a 2.76-ha area, including all living trees with a diameter at breast height (DBH) ≥ 5 cm. Aboveground biomass was estimated using an allometric equation developed for urban trees, carbon stocks were calculated using a conversion factor of 0.47, and an illustrative economic valuation was derived from a reference price in the voluntary carbon market. The inventory recorded 539 trees belonging to 68 species and 24 botanical families, with native species accounting for 79.0% of the individuals. Total aboveground biomass was estimated at 95.09 Mg (34.45 Mg ha⁻¹), corresponding to 44.69 Mg of carbon (16.19 Mg C ha⁻¹) and 163.88 Mg CO₂e. The illustrative economic valuation of the stored carbon was US$3,349.64. Native species accounted for 86.46% of the estimated carbon stock, with Moquilea tomentosa and Handroanthus impetiginosus among the main contributors. The 2024 El Niño event caused widespread flooding, affecting critical infrastructure and highlighting the urgent need for effective mitigation strategies. This study evaluates three flood management approaches using the HEC-RAS model: (1) modified channels as grey infrastructure, (2) soil organic matter enhancement and reforestation as Nature-based Solutions, and (3) a hybrid strategy. items.samenvatting_bron: This study examines how users and urban design experts perceive the ecological aesthetics of Karşıyaka Peynircioğlu Stream Park in İzmir, Türkiye, identifying convergences and divergences. A qualitative case study design draws on field observations, walking interviews, and semi-structured expert interviews. Water elements, native vegetation, and green continuity enhance aesthetic experience and place attachment for both groups, evoking everyday experiences among users while being interpreted by experts as intentional design strategies; maintenance gaps, however, weaken these perceptions. items.titel: Making Room for the Wadi: A Review of Urban Flash-Flood Resilience and Water-Sensitive Design in Saudi Cities, with a Layered Framework for Flood-Resilient Public Space
items.samenvatting_bron: Flash floods are rare in Saudi cities, but when they come they are fast, deep and deadly. The Jeddah floods of November 2009 and January 2011 killed more than a hundred people, and the storm of 24 November 2022 delivered 179.7 mm of rain in about eight hours, the highest total ever recorded in the city. This review brings together peer-reviewed and official evidence on urban flash-flood risk in western Saudi Arabia, with Jeddah and the Makkah region as the main case and Riyadh as a comparison. It covers the documented flood events and rainfall regime, hydrological and GIS studies of the urban wadis, the growth of the cities into their floodplains, the engineering response of dams, channels and forecasting, and the evidence on water-sensitive urban design (WSUD), sustainable drainage and nature-based solutions in arid regions, including the restoration of Wadi Hanifah in Riyadh. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes the Wadi-to-Plot (W2P) framework. items.titel: Multiscale climate vulnerability assessment in São Paulo state for climate adaptation planning
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change poses significant challenges to densely populated and economically dynamic regions. This study presents an integrated assessment of climate vulnerability across municipalities in São Paulo State, Brazil, combining climatic indicators, socio-environmental conditions, public health data, and institutional capacity variables. Using multivariate statistical techniques and spatial analysis, a Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) was developed to identify patterns of exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. Results reveal strong spatial heterogeneity, with clusters of high vulnerability associated with elevated surface temperatures, urban heat island intensity, socio-economic disparities, and limited institutional preparedness. Conversely, municipalities with stronger governance structures and environmental planning instruments exhibited lower vulnerability levels. The findings highlight the critical role of integrated public policies and nature-based solutions in strengthening climate resilience. This research provides a replicable framework for subnational vulnerability assessment and supports evidence-based decision-making for climate adaptation planning.

Nu kampt de ijsbaan volgens Siderius met dezelfde storing. De Elfstedenhal blijft in ieder geval dicht tot maandag. Kleine hoeveelheid De directeur benadrukt bij Omrop Fryslân dat niemand in gevaar is geweest. Deze keer ontsnapte er volgens hem maar een kleine hoeveelheid ammoniak, en het lek werd direct ontdekt. "Bij lekkage gaat er direct een alarm af bij de technische dienst", zegt Siderius. "Die krijgen dan een rood scherm te zien. items.samenvatting_bron: De toekomst van het minderheidskabinet CDA-leider Henri Bontenbal wil er de komende week "alles aan doen" om het belastingplan van het minderheidskabinet aan een meerderheid te helpen. Dat zei hij op het CDA-congres in Almere, aan de vooravond van wat een spannende week voor de coalitie van D66, CDA en VVD gaat worden. Want een meerderheid in de Tweede Kamer lijkt misschien wel in zicht, maar in de Eerste Kamer allerminst. We zijn vandaag in Almere. Hybride oorlog Al zijn we niet in oorlog, deze week werd eens duidelijk dat Europa ontzettend kwetsbaar is voor dreiging van buiten. Met gehackte koelingen in meerdere Europese supermarkten en bij Franse bloedbanken, en (valse) bommeldingen bij vliegtuigen. De lange lijst van sabotageacties, hacks en andere aanvallen in Europa zijn een bron van grote zorg. De incidenten worden ook steeds gevaarlijker. Te gast is veiligheidsexpert Bart van den Berg van Instituut Clingendael. Bruggen mogelijk langer mee Nederlandse bruggen zijn verouderd en om ze op te knappen is tot 2039 zo'n 75 miljard euro nodig. Maar zoveel geld is er niet. De TU Delft hoopt met een nieuwe aanpak beter te kunnen meten hoe slecht in dit geval de Zeelandbrug er écht aan toe is. Rijkswaterstaat kijkt met interesse naar het project in Zeeland. Maar meten.... dat houdt de rot niet tegen.

items.titel: Meer mensen met verward gedrag, drukken op hulpverlening en rechtspraak
items.samenvatting_bron: De overlast van mensen met verward gedrag neemt elk jaar toe. Moest de politie in 2015 nog ruim 66.000 keer in actie komen, vorig jaar was dat al bijna 170.000 keer. Ook dit jaar, gekeken naar de cijfers tot september, loopt het aantal meldingen weer op, met een tussenstand van 149.519 incidenten. Strafrechters Elmy Elderman en Joyce de Ruiter van de rechtbank Overijssel zijn bezorgd over dit toenemende probleem in de maatschappij. "Wij kunnen het niet oplossen. Bestuurders denken: zet ze maar vast, dan zijn ze van de straat. Maar daarna komen ze terug op straat, onbehandeld en zonder zorg", legt De Ruiter uit. Het gaat om een kleine groep mensen met ernstige psychiatrische problemen, vaak in combinatie met een verslaving. Koepelorganisatie Raad voor de rechtspraak onderschrijft wat de twee strafrechters aankaarten. Naakt over straat Vaak gaat het om kleine vergrijpen, van winkeldiefstal tot naakt over straat lopen, schreeuwen en de deur van de nachtopvang slopen, maar de druk op de hulpverlening en het rechtssysteem is er groot door. Strafrechter Elderman: "Met dit soort incidenten is de hele strafketen druk: politie, justitie, reclassering en tot slot de gevangenissen. En we zien deze mensen vaak weer terug." items.titel: Wegen worden steeds drukker en files nemen toe: 'Reistijd wordt onvoorspelbaar'
items.samenvatting_bron: De Nederlandse infrastructuur heeft dringend onderhoud nodig. Vanwege geldgebrek kunnen niet alle problemen worden aangepakt en zijn veel nieuwe projecten geschrapt. Reizigers en weggebruikers lijken hierdoor een perfecte storm van files en vertraging tegemoet te gaan, maar experts zien uitwegen en oplossingen.

items.titel: De bever is geheim wapen tegen droogte: 'Anders zou hier geen druppel staan'
items.samenvatting_bron: De steeds drogere zomers in Europa hebben grote gevolgen voor de natuur. Maar de natuur kan ook een handje helpen om in droge tijden tóch water vast te houden. In Oostenrijk werken mensen samen met de bever om tal van soorten te beschermen tegen uitdroging.
